prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling reactions
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: B003 remains my first choice. Ligand-enabled Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling turned aryl amine formation from a harsh, narrow transformation into a routine, predictable operation. It is used daily in pharmaceutical process and discovery chemistry and in materials synthesis, and it appears in countless total syntheses. The conceptual advance is ligand design guided by mechanism, and the attribution is clean: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general methods independently and in parallel, and are always credited together. Thirty years of independent confirmation leave no maturity doubt. Having read the openings, I also recognise that five of eight colleagues place B024 in their top three and that none of the other shortlisted candidates has comparable cross-committee support. I therefore propose pairing B003 with B024 credited to Liu alone. The base editors are chemically defined reagents: a deaminase performing a specific nucleobase transformation, programmed by a Cas nickase, with a clear mechanism and a rapid path to clinical use. A Liu-only credit keeps the union at three people, matches the argument made by Aqvist and Sparr, and avoids a priority fight with Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) that I cannot resolve from the shortlist alone.
statement.case_against: Against B003: the 2010 prize for Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling may make some colleagues see C-N coupling as an extension of recognised chemistry, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a real precursor, so the third-seat question is not trivial. Against pairing with B024: the new chemistry in base editing is largely protein engineering and directed evolution of deaminases on top of the 2020 CRISPR prize. A two-achievement prize also mixes a classical synthetic method with a genome-engineering tool, which may read as a prize without a unifying theme. Crediting Liu alone leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who wrote the two decisive papers, and a Liu-only credit can look like it demotes the first authors. I hold the pairing loosely and would still back B003 alone if the committee prefers a single coherent achievement.

responses.point: Linke ranks B024 first because base editing is a clear, explainable principle that created a new capability, with a full chain from mechanism to clinical trials, and he proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli.
responses.response: I accept the capability and clinical argument, and it moves me from leaving B024 off my own list to supporting it as a second part. I do not accept it as an unqualified chemistry prize. What is new chemically is the evolved deaminase and the editor architecture, while the cytidine and adenosine deamination themselves are old chemistry. I still doubt that Komor and Gaudelli must take two of the three seats. If B003 takes two, only one seat remains, and I would give it to Liu as the conceptual driver. Heiner, if you want all three trainees credited, B024 would need to be the whole prize, and I would then argue for B003 as the better chemistry on a stand-alone basis.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks PROTACs first, as a new chemical modality built on a simple induced-proximity idea, and ranks B024 second with Liu as the decisive originator.
responses.response: I agree with Johan that Liu alone is a clean B024 credit, and I share his view that the base editing chemistry is distinct from the 2020 CRISPR work. I part from him on B009. Induced proximity is simple and elegant, but no PROTAC is approved. The credit also splits into at least two lineages, PROTACs (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon-based glues (Handa), which a three-name prize merges awkwardly. I keep B009 as a first alternative for a later year, not as a lead this year. By contrast, B003 has both a clean attribution and decades of demonstrated use.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks nitrogenase first, as a mature structure-plus-mechanism achievement by Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, and ranks B003 third, calling it transformative with stable interpretation.
responses.response: I appreciate Peter's support for B003 and agree that the 2010 prize lowers novelty only slightly. On nitrogenase, I recognise that the structural and kinetic work is mature and of high quality, and I keep B038 as an alternative. My reservation is the attribution: the three-seat limit leaves out Dean and Ribbe, and the discovery is a long-running programme in which the cofactor catalytic cycle remains debated. Peter, I would want to know whether you think the carbide and cofactor-structure results can be set apart as a single definable discovery, since I could not make that case from the shortlist alone.

responses.point: Zou ranks dye-sensitized solar cells first (Gratzel, O'Regan) and also supports B003 at rank 4 as a general, predictable method whose novelty is tempered by the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I agree with Xiaodong that B003 is broad and robust, and that the 2010 overlap tempers urgency but not substance. I disagree on B025 as the top choice, because the DSSC is a materials concept whose practical impact has stayed niche and which perovskites have largely overtaken. I would put perovskites and dye cells together as a materials question for another year. If the committee wants a materials part, I would want to see a clearer argument on whether the lasting contribution is the architecture or the dyes.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Kosugi's precursor work as a priority issue rather than a claim to a third seat in B003.
Whether crediting only Liu in B024 is defensible, given that Komor and Gaudelli wrote the two foundational papers and Kondo and Nishida reported Target-AID independently.
Whether a two-part prize combining a classical synthetic method and a genome-engineering tool is acceptable, or whether the committee would rather give a single achievement.
How much the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the 2020 CRISPR prize each weigh against their later follow-on topics.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I am a synthetic organic chemist at Lund and have no recorded link to Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu or the other credited names. Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr sit on the committee, but none of the shortlisted candidates is tied to Lund University in the supplied materials.
